web_title: 2. What the Company Does: ETF Wrapper Mechanics, Operating Segments & Real-World Examples
book_title: Chapter 2: Inside the Wrapper and Across the Server Racks

epigraph.quote: To know what you own, you must follow both the legal contract in your brokerage account and the physical megawatts at the end of the power line.
epigraph.author: Infrastructure Underwriting Principle

web_blocks.html: Because NBIL is a single-stock leveraged exchange-traded fund, mapping what the company does requires inspecting two distinct operational layers. At the top layer, GraniteShares 2x Long NBIS Daily ETF (NBIL) holds just 4 portfolio positions as of November 2026 [1][59]. Rather than holding physical NBIS shares in a margin account, NBIL enters into over-the-counter Total Return Swaps (TRS) backed by cash and U.S. Treasury Bills. Both its audited June 30, 2026 N-CSR ($187.54 million notional; $391.35 million fair value) and August 31, 2026 NPORT-P show 100% single-counterparty reliance on Clear Street, LLC, with FLEX options and GraniteShares Short Term Box ETF (LBOX) as backup liquidity [2][18][42]. Clear Street pays NBIL twice the daily return of NBIS, while NBIL pays a floating financing rate of OBFR01 plus 600 bps alongside its 1.41% net expense ratio and 1.45% estimated indirect swap cost [1][2][42][43].

Beneath the swap contract sits the actual economic engine: Nebius Group N.V. (NBIS), which operates three consolidated segments—Nebius AI Cloud, Avride, and TripleTen—alongside equity-method stakes in Toloka AI and ClickHouse [4][15]. In practice, Nebius Group has converged into a single-engine AI infrastructure business. By Q3 2026, the core Nebius AI Cloud segment generated $973.8 million out of $980.8 million in total consolidated revenue, representing roughly 99.3% of the group's top line [17][20].

web_blocks.takeaway: While Avride, TripleTen, Toloka, and ClickHouse provide valuable optionality and balance-sheet asset backing, Nebius Group's operational destiny—and therefore 100% of NBIL's daily variance—is driven by Nebius AI Cloud.

web_blocks.html: 1. Nebius AI Cloud (Core Engine): Nebius builds full-stack AI infrastructure across Europe (Mäntsälä and Lappeenranta in Finland, Paris, Iceland, and the UK) and the United States (Vineland, New Jersey; Kansas City, Missouri; and Alabama) [16][25]. Nebius pairs dense NVIDIA GPU clusters (H100, H200, Blackwell B200/GB200/GB300, and planned Vera Rubin systems) with InfiniBand/NVLink fabric and its proprietary orchestration software, including Soperator—an open-source Kubernetes operator for Slurm job scheduling [14][16][26]. As a concrete enterprise example, Shopify uses Nebius H200 clusters with SkyPilot and NVIDIA Megatron Bridge to pre-train foundation models and structure merchant catalogs for AI shopping agents [21]. Similarly, Cloudflare taps Nebius compute for edge inference on Workers API, while Mistral AI and Prosus run frontier training workloads [27]. At the hyperscaler tier, Microsoft signed a five-year, $17.4B–$19.4B deal in Vineland, New Jersey, and Meta followed in March 2026 with a five-year deal worth up to $27B ($12B dedicated plus $15B backstop) [13][14][16].

2. Avride (Autonomous Vehicles & Delivery Robotics): Incubated inside Yandex's self-driving division before the 2024 carve-out, Avride develops autonomous passenger vehicles and electric sidewalk delivery robots [22][28]. In October 2025, Uber and Nebius committed up to $375 million in strategic funding and milestones to scale Avride across Uber, followed by an expansion onto Grubhub [22][23]. In daily operation, a diner in Austin, Dallas, or Jersey City orders lunch through Uber Eats or Grubhub, and a restaurant loads the meal into an Avride delivery pod. The robot navigates sidewalks autonomously using LiDAR and computer vision, crosses intersections, and texts the customer a code upon arrival, having already logged hundreds of thousands of deliveries [22][23].

3. TripleTen (Tech Reskilling Edtech): TripleTen is a consolidated online bootcamp subsidiary offering mentor-guided programs in software engineering, data science, business intelligence analytics, and quality assurance [4][9]. In a typical learner journey, a career-switcher in the U.S. or Latin America completes a 5-to-9-month part-time curriculum with code reviews to become a junior developer or data analyst. Within Nebius Group, TripleTen operates as a self-contained cash-efficiency unit focused on trimming burn rather than consuming hyperscale capital [9].

4. Deconsolidated & Equity-Method Assets (Toloka AI & ClickHouse): Two affiliated assets sit outside consolidated revenue. Toloka AI provides human-in-the-loop data labeling, reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF), and red-teaming evaluations for foundation-model builders [15][21]. Following a Q2 2025 third-party financing round, Nebius ceased to hold majority voting power and reclassified Toloka to equity-method accounting [15]. Nebius also holds a minority stake in columnar SQL leader ClickHouse, whose FY2025 mark-to-market revaluation generated a $598.9 million non-cash gain that lifted GAAP net income despite a $(611.7) million operating loss [24][29]. While these stakes offer theoretical monetization optionality, they contribute zero recurring operating cash flow to Nebius's consolidated P&L.

How NBIL Translates Segment Results Into Daily Swap Flows: NBIL holds a Clear Street Total Return Swap and U.S. Treasury collateral, with zero direct claim on Avride's robots or ClickHouse's licenses [1][42]. Instead, NBIL settles daily against the closing market return of NBIS shares. In addition, Q3 2026 Form 6-K Note 4 exposes acute customer and supplier concentration underneath that top line [48]. Three unnamed customers—Customer E (33%), Customer D (22%), and Customer C (15%)—generated 70% of Q3 2026 revenue ($980.8 million) [48]. Customer D alone accounted for 75% and Customer E 10% (85% combined) of Nebius's $4,039.9 million accounts receivable balance, while gross CapEx relied on just three hardware suppliers [48]. If one concentrated client delays acceptance or a single-dealer Clear Street swap faces margin friction during a 45%–50% gap, NBIL absorbs twice the equity shock at 4:00 PM ET [2][5][42].

web_blocks.title: Accounting vs. Operating Reality in NBIS's Bottom Line
paragraphs: Investors analyzing Nebius Group must distinguish between operating cash generation and non-cash equity revaluations. In FY2025, Nebius posted a GAAP operating loss of $(611.7) million on $529.8 million of revenue, yet reported $82.5 million in GAAP net income primarily because of a $598.9 million ClickHouse revaluation gain and discontinued-operations effects [24][29]. NBIL's daily swap tracks the equity's market reaction to both real cloud bookings and non-operating accounting noise.

book_paragraphs: If you want to understand what you are actually exposed to when you hold NBIL, you have to trace two completely different sets of plumbing. The first set of plumbing is inside the GraniteShares ETF itself. If you opened NBIL's audited June 30, 2026 Schedule of Investments, you would not see a diversified basket of stocks or even multiple Wall Street swap dealers. You would see U.S. Treasury Bills paired with a single over-the-counter total return swap written 100 percent with Clear Street, LLC, carrying a floating financing rate of the Overnight Bank Funding Rate plus 600 basis points—six full percentage points of spread on top of short-term interest rates—plus the fund's 1.41 percent net operating expense ratio and 1.45 percent estimated indirect swap cost. Every afternoon, that single-counterparty swap settles the day's score. If Nebius Group shares rise five percent, Clear Street owes the fund ten percent on that notional exposure, minus swap financing and fund fees. If Nebius drops ten percent, the fund loses twenty percent.

The second set of plumbing is the actual operating business of Nebius Group N.V., and here the story has consolidated at breathtaking speed. When Nebius re-listed in 2024, investors often treated it as a sum-of-the-parts tech incubator housing four different startups. By the third quarter of 2026, that framing was obsolete. Out of 980.8 million dollars in quarterly group revenue, Nebius AI Cloud generated 973.8 million dollars—more than ninety-nine percent of the entire enterprise.

Let us look at what Nebius AI Cloud actually does for a real customer, because "GPU-as-a-Service" sounds abstract until you watch a workload run. Take Shopify. To make millions of independent merchants' product catalogs intelligible to modern AI shopping assistants, Shopify's machine learning teams need to pre-train and fine-tune massive foundation models. They burst those heavy training jobs onto Nebius's NVIDIA H200 clusters using tools like SkyPilot and NVIDIA Megatron Bridge, relying on Nebius's low-latency InfiniBand networking and its open-source Soperator software—a clever bridge that lets classic Slurm supercomputing schedulers run seamlessly inside elastic Kubernetes pods. When a single GPU in a thousand-chip cluster throws a hardware error, Soperator automatically drains and replaces the faulty node so a multi-week training run does not crash.

book_subsections.title: The Hyperscaler Anchor and the Other Three Pillars
paragraphs: Alongside enterprise developers like Shopify, Cloudflare, and Mistral AI, Nebius transformed its scale by becoming an overflow and dedicated capacity builder for the world's largest tech giants. In Vineland, New Jersey, Nebius is commissioning massive Blackwell GPU clusters under a five-year, 17.4 to 19.4 billion dollar contract with Microsoft. In March 2026, Meta signed an even larger five-year agreement worth up to 27 billion dollars, combining 12 billion dollars of dedicated capacity with a 15 billion dollar backstop commitment.

What about the other businesses in the Nebius ecosystem? Avride, the autonomous robotics spinout, has become a tangible commercial operator in its own right. Backed by a 375 million dollar strategic commitment from Uber and Nebius in October 2025, Avride's four-wheeled electric delivery robots now roll down sidewalks in Austin, Dallas, and Jersey City, delivering hot meals for both Uber Eats and Grubhub. Picture a college student or downtown office worker ordering lunch on Grubhub: the restaurant places the order inside an autonomous Avride pod, the pod navigates curbs and crosswalks using LiDAR and computer vision, and the customer unlocks the lid with a phone code. TripleTen, the online coding bootcamp, continues to train career-switchers in software engineering, data science, and quality assurance over five-to-nine-month mentored cohorts while working to trim its own cash burn.

Meanwhile, two of the group's most famous assets—the Toloka AI data-labeling platform and the ClickHouse columnar database—no longer sit inside consolidated revenue at all. Toloka was deconsolidated in the second quarter of 2025 after a third-party investment diluted Nebius's voting control, and ClickHouse sits on the balance sheet as a minority equity stake whose 598.9 million dollar paper revaluation in 2025 masked a 611.7 million dollar core operating loss. For you and me, the takeaway is straightforward: those equity stakes are nice balance-sheet cushions if Nebius ever sells them to buy more GPUs, but NBIL's daily swap only cares about how the market prices Nebius AI Cloud.

book_subsections.title: Why Swap Counterparties and Reset Clocks Matter More Than Robot Deliveries
paragraphs: It is easy to get romantic about autonomous delivery robots rolling down sidewalks in Austin or Dallas, or about ClickHouse powering real-time analytics for global software teams. Those are genuinely impressive engineering businesses. Yet from the perspective of NBIL, they are background noise. Because NBIL's four holdings consist purely of total return swaps and Treasury collateral tied to NBIS stock, the ETF has no direct claim on Avride's fleet or ClickHouse's equity.

Every afternoon at four o'clock Eastern Time, the swap desk marks NBIS to market and settles the day's leveraged gain or loss. And Q3 2026 footnote disclosures reveal just how concentrated the underlying revenue engine remains: three unnamed customers generated 70 percent of Q3 revenue—led by Customer E at 33 percent, Customer D at 22 percent, and Customer C at 15 percent—while Customer D alone owed 75 percent of Nebius's 4.04 billion dollars in accounts receivable and capital expenditure depended on just three suppliers. If Nebius AI Cloud reports a delay in commissioning Blackwell racks in New Jersey, or if a concentrated customer delays a milestone payment, NBIL absorbs twice the equity shock instantly—all channeled through a single swap counterparty, Clear Street, LLC, with no dealer backup active on the books.

Let us also be crystal clear about how Nebius's three consolidated segments and two unconsolidated equity stakes fit together operationally. Nebius AI Cloud is the voracious capital consumer: it buys the NVIDIA H100, H200, and Blackwell clusters, leases the power substations in Finland, France, New Jersey, Missouri, and Alabama, and hires the systems engineers who maintain Soperator. Avride and TripleTen, by contrast, are self-contained operating units—Avride backed by Uber's 375 million dollar partnership, and TripleTen running lean online coding cohorts. Meanwhile, Toloka AI and ClickHouse sit off to the side as unconsolidated equity stakes. Understanding that separation prevents you from making a classic analyst mistake: never confuse a one-time paper revaluation in ClickHouse with recurring operating cash flow from renting GPUs.

Walk through one more concrete customer workflow so you can feel the difference between Nebius and a generic server landlord. When Cloudflare integrates Nebius capacity to support inference-at-the-edge through its Workers developer ecosystem, or when Mistral AI spins up multi-node frontier training clusters, they are not just renting bare concrete and electricity. They are relying on Nebius's pre-tuned InfiniBand fabric, unified root filesystems, and automated node-healing software to keep expensive GPU hours from sitting idle. That operational polish explains why Nebius won tier-one logos—even though those same workloads remain portable once contracts expire.

book_callouts.title: Mentor Check: Follow the 99% Revenue Engine
book_callouts.quote: Side bets make great conference slides, but a single-stock leveraged ETF lives and dies on the core revenue engine.
book_callouts.text: When you and I evaluate NBIL, Avride's delivery robots and ClickHouse's equity stake are interesting footnotes, not the driver. Ninety-nine percent of Nebius's revenue—and nearly one hundred percent of its capital expenditure—is tied to renting NVIDIA compute.
